gp.heading: Cost of Sales and Gross Margin
gp.text: Cost of sales decreased 3.4% to $1,327.9 million in 2025 compared to $1,374.8 million in 2024. The decrease was primarily due to the decrease in net sales in for 2025 compared to 2024 and the impact of ongoing profit improvement initiatives. Gross margin was 17.0% in both periods.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales and Gross Margin
cor.text: Cost of sales decreased 3.4% to $1,327.9 million in 2025 compared to $1,374.8 million in 2024. The decrease was primarily due to the decrease in net sales in for 2025 compared to 2024 and the impact of ongoing profit improvement initiatives. Gross margin was 17.0% in both periods.

oi.text: Segment operating income was $6.6 million in 2025 compared to $17.7 million 2024, and segment operating margin decreased 230 basis points in 2025 compared to 2024, driven by lower sales. In addition, restructuring and other special charges were $1.9 million in 2025 and $3.6 million in 2024. During 2025, an $8.9 million non-cash asset impairment charge was recorded to write-down the carrying value of certain assets, primarily at its forging operations in Arkansas.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense, Net
nonop.text: Interest expense, net increased to $47.5 million in 2025 compared to $47.4 million in 2024. The increase was due to higher interest on our 8.500% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 (the “2030 Notes”) that were issued in July 2025 compared to the 6.625% Senior Notes due 2027 (the “2027 Notes”), partially offset by lower average outstanding debt balances in 2025 compared to a year ago and lower borrowing rates in 2025 compared to 2024 on its Seventh Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (the “Credit Agreement”).

tax.text: Income tax expense in 2025 was $2.8 million on pre-tax income of $23.8 million, for an effective tax rate of 11.8%, which was less than the U.S. statutory rate of 21% primarily as a result of the tax benefit of the research and development tax credit.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: In 2025, we generated positive operating cash flow of $42.3 million compared to $35.0 million in 2024. Cash flow from operating activities was higher in 2025 due to lower working capital needs, which more than offset lower profitability in 2025.

wc.text: Cash provided by financing activities in 2025 included net debt borrowings of $6.7 million to fund capital expenditures and working capital needs. In addition, Park-Ohio issued the 2030 Notes and used the net proceeds, along with cash on hand, to redeem all of the outstanding 2027 Notes, which resulted in a cash outlay of $6.5 million for debt refinancing fees and expenses. We also made cash dividend payments totaling $7.8 million.

capex.text: Capital expenditures were $40.3 million in 2025 and $31.4 million in 2024. These capital expenditures were primarily for growth initiatives, including information technology investments across all three of our segments, and to maintain existing operations.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Net sales were $1,599.1 million in 2025 compared to $1,656.2 million in 2024, a decrease of 3.4%. The decrease was primarily due to lower customer demand in each of our business segments.

The factors explaining the changes in segment net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024 are contained in the “Segment Results” section below.

Engineered Products Segment.text: During 2025, the Company recorded non-cash asset impairment charges in its Engineered Products segment totaling $8.9 million to write-down the carrying value of certain assets, primarily at its forging operations in Arkansas.

gp.heading: Cost of Sales and Gross Margin
gp.text: Cost of sales increased to $376.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $332.0 million in the same period in 2025. The increase in cost of sales was due to the increase in net sales in the 2026 period compared to the corresponding period in 2025. Gross margin increased to 17.9% in the third quarter of 2026 from 16.7% in the corresponding 2025 period. The improvement reflected profit contribution from higher sales and continued operating initiatives across the business, including productivity improvements, automation and improved manufacturing execution.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales and Gross Margin
cor.text: Cost of sales increased to $376.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $332.0 million in the same period in 2025. The increase in cost of sales was due to the increase in net sales in the 2026 period compared to the corresponding period in 2025. Gross margin increased to 17.9% in the third quarter of 2026 from 16.7% in the corresponding 2025 period. The improvement reflected profit contribution from higher sales and continued operating initiatives across the business, including productivity improvements, automation and improved manufacturing execution.

oi.text: Segment operating income increased to $21.4 million from $17.4 million, while operating margin was 9.5% compared with 9.4% a year ago. Higher volume supported operating-income growth, alongside ongoing automation and productivity programs.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense, Net
nonop.text: Interest expense, net was $12.2 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $12.5 million in the 2025 third quarter. The decrease was due primarily to lower interest rates and lower borrowings on our revolving credit facility in the 2026 third quarter compared to the same quarter a year ago.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we generated cash of $16.9 million compared to a use of $6.4 million in the same period of 2025. Cash flow from operating activities improved in 2026 due to higher income and lower working capital needs.

wc.text: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we used net debt borrowings of $38.5 million to fund capital expenditures and working capital needs. In addition, the Company made cash dividend payments to shareholders totaling $5.4 million and payments of withholding taxes on share awards of $3.4 million.

capex.text: Capital expenditures totaled $31.9 million in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $27.6 million in the prior-year period, and supported capacity expansion, automation, existing operations and information-system implementations.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Net sales increased 15.0% to $458.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $398.6 million in the same period in 2025. This increase was primarily due to higher demand in each of our business segments.

The factors explaining the changes in segment net sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the corresponding 2025 period are contained within the “Segment Results” section below.

Supply Technologies Segment.heading: Supply Technologies Segment
Supply Technologies Segment.text:
Net sales increased 21.4% to $225.2 million, primarily reflecting higher demand for the supply-chain management business across semiconductor equipment, AI data-center infrastructure, heavy-duty truck, powersports, and aerospace and defense markets. Sales in the engineered fastener manufacturing business increased 7.9%, including demand for proprietary fastener products across multiple regions.

Segment operating income increased to $21.4 million from $17.4 million, while operating margin was 9.5% compared with 9.4% a year ago. Higher volume supported operating-income growth, alongside ongoing automation and productivity programs.

Net sales increased 12.3% in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the 2025 period due primarily to higher customer demand in certain end markets in our supply chain business, including the semiconductor, AI data center, heavy-duty truck, powersports, aerospace and defense and agricultural and industrial equipment end markets. Sales in our fastener manufacturing business were up 3.9% year-over-year.

Segment operating income was $57.4 million in the 2026 period compared to $51.5 million in the 2025 period. Operating income margin was 9.1% in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 9.2% in the 2025 period.

Engineered Products.heading: Engineered Products Segment
Engineered Products.text:
Net sales increased 11.7% to $129.7 million, reflecting demand across defense, electrical steel processing, oil and gas, agriculture, AI data-center infrastructure, semiconductor and other industrial markets. Forged and machined products sales increased 33% year over year.

Segment operating income increased to $9.1 million from $3.4 million, and operating margin improved to 7.0% from 2.9%, reflecting higher sales and improved operating execution in capital equipment and forged products. Demand for aftermarket parts and services also contributed to the segment’s activity.

Net sales were $384.8 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $354.7 million in comparable 2025 period, up 8.5%. The year-over-year increase was driven by higher customer demand across defense, electrical steel processing, oil and gas, agriculture, AI data center, semiconductor and other general industrial end markets. In our forged and machined products group, 2026 sales were up 21% compared to the corresponding 2025 period, driven by higher customer demand.

Segment operating income in the 2026 period increased by $10.6 million compared to the corresponding 2025 period, driven by higher sales and improved operational efficiencies in both our capital equipment and forged and machined products group.

Assembly Components.heading: Assembly Components Segment
Assembly Components.text: Net sales increased 6.8% to $103.6 million, primarily from higher volumes on automotive programs launched in 2025.

gp.heading: Cost of Sales and Gross Margin
gp.text: Cost of sales decreased 1% to $1,374.8 million in 2024 compared to $1,388.3 million in 2023. The decrease was driven by ongoing profit improvement initiatives and the decrease in net sales described above. Gross margin was 17.0% in 2024 compared to 16.4% in 2023. The gross margin improvement was driven by improved operating profit in our Supply Technologies segment; higher sales and improved margins in our capital equipment business; and ongoing profit improvement initiatives.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales and Gross Margin
cor.text: Cost of sales decreased 1% to $1,374.8 million in 2024 compared to $1,388.3 million in 2023. The decrease was driven by ongoing profit improvement initiatives and the decrease in net sales described above. Gross margin was 17.0% in 2024 compared to 16.4% in 2023. The gross margin improvement was driven by improved operating profit in our Supply Technologies segment; higher sales and improved margins in our capital equipment business; and ongoing profit improvement initiatives.

oi.text: Segment operating income in 2024 decreased $1.4 million compared to 2023, and segment operating margin decreased 40 basis points in 2024 compared to 2023, as a result of higher operating costs in our forged and machined products business, partially offset by the higher sales and improved margins in our capital equipment business. In addition, restructuring and other special charges were $3.6 million in 2024 and $4.9 million in 2023.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense, Net
nonop.text: Interest expense, net increased to $47.4 million in 2024 compared to $45.1 million in 2023. The increase was due to higher average interest rates partially offset by lower average outstanding borrowings in 2024 compared to 2023. Our average effective borrowing rate was 7.0% in 2024 compared to 6.6% in 2023.

tax.text: Income tax expense in 2024 was $4.9 million on pre-tax income of $44.4 million, for an effective tax rate of 11.0%, which was less than the U.S. statutory rate of 21%, primarily as a result of the tax benefit of the research and development tax credit and the release of certain valuation allowances.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: In 2024, we generated positive operating cash flow of $35.0 million compared to $53.4 million in 2023. Cash flow from operating activities was lower in 2024 due to higher working capital needs, which more than offset higher profitability in 2024.

wc.text: Our liquidity needs are primarily for working capital and capital expenditures. Our primary sources of liquidity have been cash provided by operations, funds available from existing bank credit arrangements and the sale of our debt securities. Our existing financial resources, including working capital, available bank borrowing arrangements and anticipated cash from operations, are expected to be adequate to meet anticipated cash requirements for at least the next twelve months and for the foreseeable future thereafter, including but not limited to our ability to maintain current operations and fund capital expenditure requirements, service our debt and pay dividends.

capex.text: Capital expenditures were $31.4 million in 2024 and $28.2 million in 2023. These capital expenditures were primarily for growth initiatives, including information technology investments, across all three of our segments, and to maintain existing operations.

Engineered Products Segment.text: During 2024, the Company sold real estate and other assets within its Engineered Products segment for cash proceeds of $9.3 million, resulting in a net gain of $0.8 million. The Company also sold real estate within its Assembly Components segment for cash proceeds of $2.2 million, resulting in a net gain of $1.7 million. The total net gain of $2.5 million is recorded on a separate line in the Consolidated Statements of Operations and is excluded from segment income.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 56% of Supply Technologies’ net sales were to domestic customers.

The five largest customers, to which Supply Technologies sells through sole-source contracts to multiple operating divisions or locations, accounted for approximately 36% and 34% of the sales of Supply Technologies in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 61% of Assembly Components’ net sales were to domestic customers.

Approximately 49% of our induction heating and melting systems’ revenues are derived from the sale of replacement parts and provision of field service, primarily for the installed base of our own products.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 57% of Engineered Products’ net sales were to domestic customers.
We derived 32% and 7% of our net sales during the year ended December 31, 2025 from the automotive and heavy-duty truck industries, respectively.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, our ten largest customers accounted for approximately 25% of our net sales.

During 2025 and 2024, sales to these customers amounted to approximately $ 200.4 million and $ 235.9 million, respectively, which represented approximately 13 % and 14 %, respectively, of the Company’s net sales.
Over time arrangements represented approximately 19 % of the Company's total consolidated sales for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Total Supply Management ™ is typically provided to customers pursuant to sole-source arrangements.
We administer the processes customized to each customer’s needs by replacing numerous current suppliers with a sole-source relationship with Supply Technologies.

Our sole-source arrangements foster long-term, entrenched supply relationships with our customers and, as a result, the average tenure of service for our top 50 Supply Technologies clients exceeds ten years.
These sales, across multiple operating divisions, are through sole-source contracts.
We rely on several key customers.
Our Supply Technologies business depends upon third parties for substantially all of our component parts.
We depend upon the ability of these suppliers, among other things, to meet stringent performance and quality specifications and to conform to delivery schedules.

We also depend on our information technology systems to maintain confidential, proprietary and personal information relating to our current, former and prospective employees, customers and other third parties in these systems and in systems of third-party providers who we engage in connection with the processing and storage of certain information.

Our success depends upon the efforts, abilities and expertise of our executive officers and other senior managers, including Matthew Crawford, our Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and President, as well as the president of each of our operating units.
Our primary sources of liquidity have been cash provided by operations, funds available from existing bank credit arrangements and the sale of our debt securities.
Estimating probable losses requires the analysis of multiple forecasted factors that often depend on judgments and potential actions by third parties.
